steps.business_rule: This step initialises two VSAM KSDS (Key-Sequenced Data Set) work files used in a wire transfer processing workflow. It unconditionally deletes any pre-existing versions of the INPUT and EXTRACT work clusters (using PURGE to bypass expiry dates), suppresses non-fatal delete errors (condition codes 8 or below are tolerated), then re-creates both clusters with fixed 200-byte records keyed on a 16-byte field starting at offset 0. The INPUT cluster is allocated larger initial space (20 cylinders) than the EXTRACT cluster (10 cylinders), reflecting that the input dataset is expected to hold more raw data before extraction processing reduces it. This is a classic DELETE-DEFINE initialisation pattern to ensure clean, empty work files at the start of each batch run.

key_fields.meaning: Primary key for WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS — a 16-byte character field starting at the first byte of each 200-byte record, likely a wire transfer reference or transaction identifier used to uniquely identify and sequence input records

Primary key for WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS — the same 16-byte character key structure applied to the extract work cluster, indicating extracted wire transfer records share the same key domain as input records

operations.description: Delete the existing VSAM cluster WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS (including its DATA and INDEX components) using PURGE to bypass any retention or expiry date restrictions. This ensures a clean slate regardless of when the cluster was last created.
Delete the existing VSAM cluster WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS (including its DATA and INDEX components) using PURGE to bypass any retention or expiry date restrictions.

Condition code check: IF LASTCC > 8 THEN SET MAXCC = 0. This suppresses errors up to and including condition code 8 (which IDCAMS issues when a dataset to be deleted does not exist). Condition codes of 4 (warnings) and 8 (dataset not found) are tolerated so the job does not abend on first run or after a clean environment. Only condition codes above 8 (genuine errors) would cause downstream failure.

Create a new empty VSAM KSDS cluster WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS with fixed-length 200-byte records, a 16-byte key at offset 0, primary allocation of 20 cylinders with 5 cylinder secondary extents, and SHAREOPTIONS(2 3) allowing multiple readers in the same system and unrestricted cross-system access. Separate DATA (WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS.DATA) and INDEX (WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS.INDEX) components are named explicitly.

Create a new empty VSAM KSDS cluster WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS with fixed-length 200-byte records, a 16-byte key at offset 0, primary allocation of 10 cylinders with 5 cylinder secondary extents, and SHAREOPTIONS(2 3). Separate DATA (WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS.DATA) and INDEX (WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS.INDEX) components are named explicitly. Smaller initial allocation than the INPUT cluster reflects expected data reduction after extraction filtering.

steps.pyspark_hint:
# VSAM KSDS initialisation has no direct PySpark equivalent; modern analogue is dropping and recreating Delta/Hive tables or clearing a managed storage path.
# e.g.: spark.sql('DROP TABLE IF EXISTS wire_work_input'); spark.sql('CREATE TABLE wire_work_input (key STRING, record STRING) USING DELTA LOCATION "/mnt/wire/work/input"')
steps.notes: 1. MIGRATION PATTERN: This is a pure infrastructure initialisation step. In a modern platform (Databricks, GCS, ADLS, S3) the equivalent is DROP/CREATE of a managed table or deletion and recreation of a storage prefix — no data transformation occurs here. 2. SHAREOPTIONS(2 3): Option 2 for the same-system share level means multiple jobs can read simultaneously but only one can write; cross-system (option 3) allows full sharing. Migrated solution should implement equivalent concurrency controls (e.g., Delta Lake optimistic concurrency or table locking). 3. KEY OFFSET: IDCAMS KEYS(16 0) means length=16, offset=0 (zero-based), so the key occupies bytes 1-16 in 1-based terms. The key is almost certainly a wire transfer transaction ID or reference number. 4. FIXED RECORD SIZE: RECORDSIZE(200 200) with equal minimum and maximum confirms strictly fixed-length records — no variable-length handling needed in migration; map directly to fixed-width schema with exactly 200 bytes per record. 5. PURGE FLAG: The use of PURGE on both DELETEs is significant — it means expiry dates are actively being set on these clusters elsewhere (possibly in the DEFINE or via SMS). Ensure the modern equivalent does not have retention policies that would block recreation. 6. ERROR SUPPRESSION LOGIC: The IF LASTCC > 8 / SET MAXCC = 0 idiom is a standard mainframe pattern for 'ignore dataset not found'. In a Python/PySpark migration, implement as a try/except around the drop operation, catching only 'table not found' or 'path not found' exceptions. 7. CYLINDERS allocation (20 and 10) is mainframe-specific storage sizing; no direct equivalent needed in cloud storage but capacity planning should account for estimated record counts at 200 bytes each.
steps.sysin_content:
DELETE WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS  CLUSTER PURGE
  DELETE WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS  CLUSTER PURGE
  IF LASTCC > 8 THEN
    SET MAXCC = 0
  DEFINE CLUSTER                           -
    (NAME(WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS)            -
     INDEXED                               -
     KEYS(16 0)                            -
     RECORDSIZE(200 200)                   -
     CYLINDERS(20 5)                       -
     SHAREOPTIONS(2 3))                    -
  DATA                                     -
    (NAME(WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS.DATA))      -
  INDEX                                    -
    (NAME(WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS.INDEX))
  DEFINE CLUSTER                           -
    (NAME(WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS)            -
     INDEXED                               -
     KEYS(16 0)                            -
     RECORDSIZE(200 200)                   -
     CYLINDERS(10 5)                       -
     SHAREOPTIONS(2 3))                    -
  DATA                                     -
    (NAME(WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS.DATA))      -
  INDEX                                    -
    (NAME(WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS.INDEX))

steps.business_rule: This step loads a sequential flat file containing daily wire transfer input records into a VSAM Key-Sequenced Data Set (KSDS). The REPRO command copies all records from the sequential input file (WIRE.DAILY.INPUT.SEQ) into the VSAM KSDS work dataset (WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS), making the data available for subsequent keyed-access processing. This is a standard staging pattern used in batch payment pipelines to convert flat file input into an indexed VSAM structure for efficient record retrieval by downstream steps.

key_fields.meaning: KSDS prime key — exact offset and length are not defined in this JCL step; they are defined in the VSAM KSDS cluster definition (DEFINE CLUSTER) and enforced automatically by VSAM when REPRO loads the records. The key must be pre-embedded in the sequential records at the position matching the cluster definition.

operations.description: IDCAMS REPRO copies every record from the sequential input file SEQIN (WIRE.DAILY.INPUT.SEQ) into the VSAM KSDS VSAMOUT (WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS) with no filtering, transformation, or selection. Records are loaded in the order they appear in the sequential file; VSAM will insert them in key sequence according to the KSDS cluster definition. If the KSDS is empty this is an initial load; if it already contains records, REPRO will attempt to add or replace depending on VSAM disposition and any REPLACE/NOREPLACE parameters (NOREPLACE is the default, so duplicate keys will cause an error).

steps.pyspark_hint: df = spark.read.format('fixed_length_or_csv').load('s3://bucket/wire/daily/input/seq/'); df.write.format('delta').mode('overwrite').saveAsTable('wire_work_input_ksds')  # target table should have primary key equivalent enforced
steps.notes: 1. MIGRATION CAVEAT — KSDS key definition: The VSAM KSDS prime key offset and length are not visible in this step; they reside in the DEFINE CLUSTER control cards for WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS. These must be located and documented before migration, as they determine the unique key for the target table or store. 2. DUPLICATE KEY HANDLING: Default REPRO behaviour is NOREPLACE — a duplicate prime key will cause a non-zero return code and may abort the step. In a modern equivalent, upsert (MERGE) semantics should be considered to replicate this behaviour faithfully. 3. RECORD FORMAT: The sequential file record format (RECFM, LRECL) must be verified against the KSDS record size to ensure compatibility; mismatches cause REPRO to fail. 4. ORDERING ASSUMPTION: The sequential input file is assumed to be in ascending prime-key order. If it is not, VSAM will reject out-of-sequence records during load unless the KSDS was defined with REUSE or records are being individually inserted (non-initial-load). Validate sort order of WIRE.DAILY.INPUT.SEQ before migrating. 5. MODERN PATTERN: In a modern data platform this step maps to writing a Parquet/Delta table keyed on the wire transfer identifier, with the source flat file ingested from S3 or HDFS. A schema-on-read approach should account for the fixed-length EBCDIC record layout typical of mainframe sequential files.

steps.business_rule: This step extracts and sorts wire transfer records from a daily sequential input file. It filters the dataset to retain only records where the transaction type code at bytes 55-56 equals 'PE' (likely representing a specific wire payment entry type, e.g. 'Payment Entry' or 'Pending') AND where the transaction amount field at bytes 17-25 (packed decimal) is greater than zero — effectively excluding zero-value or null transactions. The surviving records are then sorted primarily by an 8-character reference/account key (bytes 44-51) in ascending order, and secondarily by the packed decimal amount field (bytes 17-25) in descending order, producing a ranked extract for downstream processing.

key_fields.meaning: Transaction type or payment category code — records must equal 'PE' (e.g. Payment Entry or Pending Entry wire type) to be included in the extract
Transaction amount in packed decimal format (9 bytes = up to 17 significant digits); must be greater than zero to be included — filters out zero-value or placeholder records
Primary sort key — likely a wire reference number, account identifier, or routing key (8-character alphanumeric); sorted ascending to group related wire records together

operations.description: Include only records where the 2-byte character field at offset 55 equals 'PE' AND the 9-byte packed decimal amount field at offset 17 is strictly greater than zero. Both conditions must be true simultaneously (AND logic). This removes non-PE transaction types and eliminates any zero-amount wire records before sorting.

Sort the filtered records by two keys: (1) the 8-byte character field at offset 44 in ascending order (primary key — groups records by reference/account), then (2) the 9-byte packed decimal amount at offset 17 in descending order (secondary key — within each group, largest amounts appear first). Output is written to WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.SEQ as a fixed-block file with LRECL=200.

steps.notes: 1. OFFSET CONVENTION: DFSORT uses 1-based offsets; the INCLUDE field at position 55, length 2 maps to Python slice [54:56] and the PD amount at position 17, length 9 maps to bytes [16:25]. The sort key at offset 44, length 8 maps to bytes [43:51]. 2. PACKED DECIMAL (PD): The 9-byte PD amount field can represent values up to 17 digits; migration must decode PD encoding — each byte holds two decimal digits except the last which holds one digit and the sign nibble (C=positive, D=negative, F=unsigned). Use a PD decoder in PySpark or Python before comparison and sorting. 3. ZERO FILTER: The PD GT +0 condition explicitly excludes zero and negative amounts — confirm whether negative wire amounts are valid business data that should be routed elsewhere rather than silently dropped. 4. OUTPUT FILE: WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.SEQ is a work/intermediate dataset (DISP=NEW,CATLG,DELETE) with 10 primary + 5 secondary cylinders allocated and LRECL=200 FB — this is consumed by a downstream step and should be treated as a staging table in the modern platform. 5. CONTROL CARD SOURCE: SYSIN is read from a shared PDS member SYS2.CNTL(WIREEXT) — this externalised control card pattern means the filter criteria ('PE', zero-amount threshold) may be changed without recompiling JCL; document this as a configurable business parameter in the migrated solution.

steps.business_rule: This step reads a wire transfer extract file, sorts all records in descending order by transaction amount, then splits the output into two separate files based on a threshold of 1,000,000: records with a transaction amount greater than 1,000,000 are written to a HIGH-value file (large/high-risk wire transfers), while records with a transaction amount of 1,000,000 or less are written to a LOW-value file (standard wire transfers). This supports downstream processing or risk-tiering of wire transfer transactions by value.

key_fields.meaning: Wire transfer transaction amount stored as a Packed Decimal (BCD) value; 9 bytes of packed decimal can hold up to 17 significant digits. Used as the primary sort key and the threshold split criterion (>1,000,000 vs <=1,000,000).

operations.description: Sort all input records from WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.SEQ in descending order by the 9-byte Packed Decimal transaction amount field starting at byte offset 17. The descending sort means the largest wire transfer amounts appear first in both output files.

After sorting, split the single sorted stream into two output datasets based on the transaction amount at offset 17 (9-byte PD): records where the amount is strictly greater than +1,000,000 are routed to WIRE.WORK.HIGH.SEQ (high-value wire transfers); records where the amount is less than or equal to +1,000,000 are routed to WIRE.WORK.LOW.SEQ (low-value wire transfers). Every input record is written to exactly one output file — the two INCLUDE conditions are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive for non-null amounts.
OUTFIL HIGHVAL applies INCLUDE condition: transaction amount (offset 17, 9 bytes, PD) GT +1,000,000. Only wire transfers exceeding one million units of currency pass to the high-value output file.
OUTFIL LOWVAL applies INCLUDE condition: transaction amount (offset 17, 9 bytes, PD) LE +1,000,000. Wire transfers at or below one million units of currency pass to the low-value output file.

steps.notes: 1. FIELD FORMAT — The transaction amount is Packed Decimal (PD) at offset 17 (1-based), length 9 bytes. In PySpark/Python this must be decoded from the raw binary EBCDIC-encoded packed decimal bytes; a custom UDF or library (e.g., py-ebcdic or a bespoke PD decoder) will be required when reading the flat file before any filtering or sorting can occur. 2. RECORD LENGTH — Both output files are FB LRECL=200, matching the sort input; no record reformatting occurs — full 200-byte records are written to both outputs unchanged. 3. THRESHOLD BOUNDARY — The boundary value +1,000,000 is handled correctly: GT strictly excludes 1,000,000 (goes to LOWVAL), LE includes it (goes to LOWVAL). Ensure the PySpark equivalent uses strict greater-than (>) for HIGHVAL and less-than-or-equal (<=) for LOWVAL. 4. SIGNED VALUES — PD format supports signed values. If the source data can contain negative amounts (e.g., reversals or credits), records with negative PD values will always satisfy LE +1,000,000 and route to LOWVAL. Validate business expectations for negative amounts. 5. SORT ORDER PRESERVED IN OUTPUTS — Because DFSORT sorts first and then applies OUTFIL filtering, both output files inherit the descending sort order by amount. Replicate this in PySpark by sorting before the filter/write operations. 6. SPACE ALLOCATION — Both output datasets are allocated at 5 primary + 2 secondary cylinders (FB, LRECL=200). Size the modern target accordingly based on expected record volumes. 7. EXTERNAL CONTROL CARDS — SYSIN is sourced from SYS2.CNTL(WIRESPL), a PDS member, not inline. Ensure the correct member version is used during migration validation.
steps.sysin_content:
SORT FIELDS=(17,9,PD,D)
  OUTFIL FNAMES=HIGHVAL,
         INCLUDE=(17,9,PD,GT,+1000000)
  OUTFIL FNAMES=LOWVAL,
         INCLUDE=(17,9,PD,LE,+1000000)

steps.business_rule: Straight copy of WIRE.DAILY.INPUT.SEQ to WIRE.DAILY.BACKUP.SEQ. No record transformation applied. Used for backup or audit copy creation.

operations.description: Direct record-by-record copy of entire input file to output. SYSIN DD DUMMY means no control cards — all records copied unchanged.

steps.notes: IEBGENER with SYSIN DD DUMMY is always a straight copy. Consider ICEGENER (DFSORT-based) for files > 1M records.

steps.business_rule: Non-utility program step. PGM=ACCTPAY is a custom application program (COBOL, Assembler, or PL/I). JUIA does not decode non-utility steps — review source code separately.

operations.description: Custom application logic — see program source

steps.business_rule: This step summarises wire transfer processed records by a 3-character code at position 63 (likely a currency code, wire type, or routing code). All input records from WIRE.PROCESSED.SEQ are sorted ascending by that code, and any records sharing the same code have their packed-decimal amount field (position 17, 9 bytes) summed together, collapsing multiple detail rows into a single aggregated summary row per code. The output record is then reformatted to 200 bytes, retaining key identifier fields from the original record alongside the converted (PD-to-signed-fullword) summed amount, producing a compact wire transfer summary dataset.

key_fields.meaning: Primary sort and grouping key — a 3-character alphanumeric code, likely a currency code, wire transfer type, or bank routing/channel identifier used to aggregate wire totals
Packed-decimal numeric amount field — the wire transfer monetary value being summed across all records sharing the same grouping key; accumulated total per group in the output
Leading identifier retained in output — likely an account number, transaction reference, or entity identifier from the first (or surviving) record in each group
Secondary descriptive field retained in output — possibly a date, value date, or bank identifier from the original record
Short qualifier field retained in output — possibly a transaction status code, currency minor indicator, or processing flag
Trailing 3-character field retained in output — possibly a country code, region code, or supplementary classification adjacent to the sort key

operations.description: Sort all records from WIRE.PROCESSED.SEQ in ascending order on the 3-character character field at position 63 (length 3, format CH). This groups records with the same code together in preparation for aggregation.

SUM operation: after sorting, collapse all records sharing the same value in the sort key field (pos 63, len 3) into a single output record. The packed-decimal amount field at position 17 (length 9, PD format) is arithmetically summed across all records in each group. Non-summed fields are taken from the first surviving record in each group. Duplicate group records are deleted after summation.

OUTREC reformats each surviving summary record into a new 200-byte fixed-block layout composed of: bytes 1-16 from original (16-byte identifier), bytes 63-65 from original (3-byte grouping key), the 9-byte PD amount field at position 17 converted to a signed fullword fixed-point (FS) representation expanded to 12 bytes, bytes 44-51 from original (8-byte date/bank field), bytes 55-56 from original (2-byte qualifier), and bytes 66-68 from original (3-byte trailing code). Total output width must fit within LRECL=200.

steps.pyspark_hint: df = spark.read(...); df_agg = df.groupBy('code_63_3').agg(F.sum('amount_17_9').alias('amount_17_9'), F.first('id_1_16').alias('id_1_16'), F.first('date_44_8').alias('date_44_8'), F.first('flag_55_2').alias('flag_55_2'), F.first('trail_66_3').alias('trail_66_3')).orderBy('code_63_3'); df_out = df_agg.select('id_1_16','code_63_3','amount_17_9','date_44_8','flag_55_2','trail_66_3')
steps.notes: 1. OFFSET AMBIGUITY: The OUTREC references original input record offsets per DFSORT rules (OUTREC operates on pre-sort original records, not post-INREC records), so all offsets are 1-based positions in WIRE.PROCESSED.SEQ. 2. PD-TO-FS CONVERSION: The SUM field (pos 17, 9 bytes PD) is emitted in OUTREC as TO=FS,LENGTH=12, meaning the packed-decimal accumulated total is converted to a 12-byte signed fixed-point (FS) integer representation — migration must handle this numeric type conversion explicitly; do not treat it as a raw byte copy. 3. SUM KEY vs SUM FIELD: The sort/grouping key is ONLY pos 63 len 3 (CH). The SUM card aggregates ONLY the PD field at pos 17 len 9. These are independent concerns. 4. SURVIVING RECORD: For non-SUM fields in the OUTREC (pos 1-16, 44-51, 55-56, 66-68), DFSORT retains values from the first record in each sorted group (EQUALS behaviour) — downstream consumers should be aware these descriptor fields are not aggregated and may not be representative if records vary within a group. 5. OUTPUT RECORD WIDTH: The reformatted output fields sum to 16+3+12+8+2+3=44 bytes of defined content within LRECL=200; remaining bytes are likely padded with spaces or binary zeros to fill the fixed-length record — verify padding behaviour in migration. 6. SPACE ALLOCATION: SORTOUT is allocated as NEW,CATLG with 5 primary + 2 secondary cylinders, RECFM=FB, LRECL=200 — in a modern platform this maps to a partitioned or columnar output with equivalent schema. 7. LOW-CONFIDENCE FIELD MEANINGS: Business meanings assigned to fields are inferred from context (WIRE.PROCESSED dataset name and field positions); confirmation against a copybook (COBOL record layout) is strongly recommended before migration.
steps.sysin_content:
SORT FIELDS=(63,3,CH,A)
  SUM FIELDS=(17,9,PD)
  OUTREC FIELDS=(1,16,
                 63,3,
                 17,9,PD,TO=FS,LENGTH=12,
                 44,8,
                 55,2,
                 66,3)

steps.business_rule: This step uses the IDCAMS LISTCAT utility to catalogue all metadata attributes for two VSAM KSDS (Key-Sequenced Data Set) datasets: WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS and WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS. The ALL parameter requests the full set of catalogue information including allocation, space usage, statistics, volume, and index details for each dataset. This is a diagnostic and auditing operation, commonly used to verify that these wire transfer working datasets exist in the system catalogue, confirm their physical allocation and space statistics, and document their current state — often placed at the end of a job to provide a post-processing audit trail of the VSAM files used during the wire transfer workflow.

operations.description: LISTCAT ENTRIES(WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS) ALL — reads the ICF catalogue and extracts all metadata attributes for the VSAM KSDS dataset WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS, including cluster name, data component, index component, space allocation (primary and secondary), high-used RBA, high-allocated RBA, record count, key length, key offset, CISIZE, freespace percentages, volume serial, extent information, creation date, expiry date, last-reference date, and statistics such as records inserted, deleted, updated, and retrieved. Output is written to SYSPRINT.

LISTCAT ENTRIES(WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS) ALL — reads the ICF catalogue and extracts all metadata attributes for the VSAM KSDS dataset WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS (the wire transfer extract working file), producing the same comprehensive set of catalogue statistics as above. Output is written to SYSPRINT.

steps.pyspark_hint: # No PySpark equivalent — LISTCAT is a catalogue metadata query, not a data transformation. Python equivalent: subprocess.run(['tsocmd', 'LISTCAT ENTRIES(WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS) ALL']) or call IBM z/OS REST API catalogue services endpoint for dataset attributes.
steps.notes: 1. LISTCAT is a read-only, non-destructive operation — it produces no output datasets and modifies no data; migration of this step produces only a logging/audit equivalent. 2. Both datasets are VSAM KSDS (Key-Sequenced Data Sets), meaning they are keyed-access files with an embedded index; their modern equivalents would typically be relational database tables or keyed object-store entries — the LISTCAT output would be replaced by querying table metadata (e.g., DESCRIBE TABLE or information_schema queries). 3. In a modern cloud or Spark platform, the equivalent audit step would be: record row counts, schema details, partition statistics, and storage sizes from the Delta Lake or Hive metastore for the equivalent target tables. 4. The dataset naming convention WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS and WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS confirms these are intermediate working files (WORK qualifier) within a wire transfer processing pipeline — INPUT likely holds raw incoming wire records and EXTRT holds extracted/filtered wire records ready for downstream processing. 5. No condition code logic (IF/THEN/ELSE) is present, so this step is unconditional and a non-zero return code from a missing dataset would cause the step to fail — migration should include existence checks for the target tables before running the metadata audit. 6. The ALL parameter means every available catalogue field is reported — when documenting migration, capture key fields: CISIZE, KEYLEN, key offset, FREESPACE, HI-U-RBA, and record counts as these drive the sizing of the equivalent modern dataset.
steps.sysin_content:
LISTCAT ENTRIES(WIRE.WORK.INPUT.KSDS)  ALL
  LISTCAT ENTRIES(WIRE.WORK.EXTRT.KSDS)  ALL

warnings: STEP010: validator reported 5 advisory issue(s); see validation.json

filter_logic.detail: No INCLUDE/OMIT filter logic is present in the SYSIN. The step is purely DELETE and DEFINE (initialisation). The condition code gate (IF LASTCC > 8 THEN SET MAXCC = 0) is correctly implemented in _condition_code_check(): codes <= 8 are suppressed and max_cc is reset to 0 before the DEFINE phase, exactly mirroring the SYSIN semantics. CC=8 (table not found) is tolerated; CC>8 propagates as an error.

sort_logic.detail: No sort operations are present in the SYSIN. This is a DELETE/DEFINE initialisation step only. No SORT, MERGE, or ordering control cards exist in the original IDCAMS control stream.

column_names.detail: Column names are meaningful and derived from field semantics: COL_KEY='wire_transfer_key' (maps to KEYS(16 0), 16-byte wire transfer reference), COL_RECORD='record_payload' (bytes 17-200), COL_CLUSTER_NAME, COL_RECORD_LENGTH, COL_CREATED_AT. All column names are defined as module-level constants and referenced consistently throughout, satisfying the single-definition requirement.

pd_handling.detail: No packed decimal (PD/COMP-3) fields are referenced in the SYSIN or key field definitions. Both cluster keys are defined as CH (character) format, 16 bytes at offset 0. No PD decoding is required for this step.

output_structure.detail: The function initialise_wire_transfer_work_clusters() returns a dict[str, Any] with keys: 'status', 'max_cc', 'input_table', 'extract_table', and 'operations'. This is a well-defined, documented return type suitable for downstream orchestration. The schema (KSDS_SCHEMA) correctly defines the Delta table structure: STRING NOT NULL key (16 bytes), BINARY payload (184 bytes), plus audit columns. Both INPUT (20 cylinder) and EXTRACT (10 cylinder) cluster specs are correctly differentiated. CREATE TABLE uses IF NOT EXISTS and verifies row count = 0 post-creation.

split_logic.detail: No OUTFIL split logic is present in the SYSIN. The step creates two separate clusters (INPUT and EXTRACT) but this is not a data split — they are independent empty work file initialisations, not conditional routing of records.

aggregation.detail: No SUM, GROUP BY, or aggregation operations are present in the SYSIN. This is a pure infrastructure initialisation step with no data transformation.

validation_results.synthetic_data_summary: Generated 15 synthetic wire transfer records with 16-byte keys (e.g., 'WIRE0000000000001' truncated to 16 bytes) and 184-byte payloads. Records cover: (1) normal records that would exist before DELETE and be cleanly recreated (10 records), (2) edge cases where tables do not exist prior to DELETE triggering CC=8 suppression path (3 records), (3) records with boundary key values including all-spaces and all-zeros keys (2 records). For the DELETE phase: 3 records exercise the 'table not found' CC=8 suppression path. For DEFINE phase: all 15 records validate schema adherence with 16-byte key at offset 0 and 184-byte payload. No filter/sort/aggregation records apply as this is a pure initialisation step.
issues_found: Minor: The _condition_code_check() function has an ambiguous adjusted_max calculation: 'adjusted_max = min(max_cc, last_cc) if last_cc == 0 else max_cc' — when last_cc==0 and max_cc==8, this would reduce max_cc to 0 prematurely inside the function rather than letting the explicit 'if max_cc <= 8: max_cc = 0' block in the main function handle the reset. However, since max_cc is reset unconditionally to 0 after both DELETEs complete (if max_cc <= 8), this does not affect the final outcome and the end-to-end CC suppression behaviour is correct.

Minor: The IDCAMS condition code logic 'IF LASTCC > 8 THEN SET MAXCC = 0' is applied after EACH delete individually in the code, whereas in the original SYSIN it appears as a single gate after BOTH deletes complete. The functional result is equivalent since both deletes run unconditionally and CC=8 is suppressed in both cases, but the sequencing is technically different from the original control stream.

Minor: The _condition_code_check() function returns adjusted_max using 'min(max_cc, last_cc) if last_cc == 0' which could incorrectly lower max_cc from 8 to 0 mid-stream if a CC=0 follows a CC=8. This is corrected by the explicit 'if max_cc <= 8: max_cc = 0' block later, making the net result correct but the intermediate logic within _condition_code_check is misleading.

Informational: CYLINDERS(20 5) vs CYLINDERS(10 5) allocation difference between INPUT and EXTRACT clusters is correctly implemented in the respective KsdsAllocation dataclass instances. This is a PASS but noted for completeness.

Informational: The storage path separation (input_base_path vs extract_base_path as separate parameters) correctly ensures the two Delta tables are stored at distinct locations, mirroring the separate VSAM DATA and INDEX component naming convention.

filter_logic.detail: The SYSIN contains only 'REPRO INFILE(SEQIN) OUTFILE(VSAMOUT)' with no INCLUDE, OMIT, or selection parameters. The generated code correctly applies no filtering or transformation to the records — every record from the input DataFrame is passed through to the target table. The only pre-write checks are duplicate-key detection (faithfully replicating NOREPLACE semantics) and an empty-input short-circuit, neither of which constitutes a filter in the SYSIN sense.

sort_logic.detail: The SYSIN specifies no SORT or ordering clause. IDCAMS REPRO preserves sequential file order and VSAM inserts in key sequence internally. The generated code writes records in the order they appear in the input DataFrame, which correctly mirrors mainframe behavior. The OUTREC layout is correctly implemented: bytes 1-16 identifier (rpad 16), bytes 17-19 grouping_code (rpad 3), bytes 20-31 amount_fs as lpad 12-char FS string, bytes 32-39 date_bank (rpad 8), bytes 40-41 transaction_status (rpad 2), bytes 42-44 trailing_code (rpad 3), bytes 45-200 space padding of 156 chars. aggregation.detail: The SYSIN specifies SUM FIELDS=(17,9,PD) with GROUP BY on the SORT key (63,3,CH). The code correctly groups by GROUPING_CODE and sums AMOUNT into AMOUNT_FS using F.sum(), collapsing all records sharing the same grouping_code into a single output row. Non-SUM fields (identifier, date_bank, transaction_status, trailing_code) are taken from the first record in each group using ROW_NUMBER() over a window partitioned by grouping_code and ordered by monotonically_increasing_id(), then joined back to the sum result. This correctly implements DFSORT SUM survivor semantics (first record in sorted group) deterministically, avoiding the non-determinism of F.first() after a shuffle. The join is inner, which is correct since every grouping_code in sum_df must have a corresponding first record. Overflow guards for FS12 representation are correctly implemented with appropriate thresholds (positive: 999,999,999,999; negative: -99,999,999,999).

validation_results.synthetic_data_summary: 15 synthetic wire transfer records were designed covering: 5 groups of records sharing the same grouping_code (USD, EUR, GBP) to test SUM collapse and first-record survivor semantics; 2 singleton records (JPY, CHF) to test pass-through with no aggregation needed; records with zero amounts to test boundary; a record with a negative amount to test FS sign rendering; records with amounts near the FS12 overflow boundary (999,999,999,999 and just above); a record with null/empty identifier to test coalesce in _fixed_ch; and records with grouping_codes that sort lexicographically to verify ascending order. Of the 15 records, all pass the implicit include-all condition (no INCLUDE/OMIT card). The key aggregation scenarios: 3 USD records collapse to 1 summed row, 2 EUR records collapse to 1, 2 GBP records collapse to 1, and singletons for JPY/CHF pass through. The first-record survivor is tracked by ingest sequence to validate non-SUM field retention. Overflow scenarios were checked for both positive and negative extremes.

issues_before: CORRECTNESS RISK — F.first() non-determinism: The pre-aggregation orderBy(GROUPING_CODE.asc()) does not influence which record F.first() selects within each group after groupBy(), because Spark's shuffle for groupBy destroys partition-local ordering. The surviving record for non-SUM fields (identifier, date_bank, transaction_status, trailing_code) is therefore non-deterministic and may differ from the DFSORT SUM first-record survivor on any given execution. The comment in the code acknowledges this but the pre-sort is misleadingly presented as if it aids F.first() behaviour. A window function with ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by grouping_code and ordered by a sequence/tie-break column is required for deterministic first-record fidelity.

MINOR — FS format for negative values: DFSORT PD,TO=FS,LENGTH=12 produces a signed numeric display field. For negative values, Spark's Long.cast('string') produces '-123456' which when left-padded to 12 with spaces gives '      -123456'. This places the minus sign inside the field rather than as the leading byte. A strict DFSORT FS output would also right-justify the digits with the sign immediately preceding the first digit (e.g., '      -123456'). The Spark rendering matches this convention for typical values, but if the absolute value has 12 digits the minus sign would be truncated by the substr(1,12) guard, silently corrupting large negative amounts. A runtime check or explicit overflow guard for negative values exceeding 11 digits is absent.

MINOR — substr(1,12) overflow truncation for large positives: The _amount_to_fs12() function uses lpad to 12 chars then substr(1,12). If the summed amount exceeds 12 decimal digits (> 999,999,999,999), lpad will not truncate — it pads only if shorter — so the value will exceed 12 chars and substr will silently truncate the most-significant digits, producing a wrong value with no error raised. The comment notes this risk but no runtime guard is implemented.

MINOR — _fixed_ch uses rpad (left-aligned) for all CH fields: DFSORT OUTREC CH fields are output as-is from the record (fixed-length source fields are already the correct width). The rpad approach is correct for space-padding shorter strings, but if a source field is longer than its declared width (e.g., identifier > 16 chars due to upstream data quality issues), substr(1,width) will silently truncate without warning. This is acceptable behaviour but worth noting for production validation.
correction_history.correction_hint: Replace the F.first() aggregation approach with a window-function-based first-record selection to achieve deterministic DFSORT SUM survivor semantics. Add a monotonically_increasing_id() or ingest sequence column to the input DataFrame, then use Window.partitionBy(GROUPING_CODE).orderBy(sequence_col) with ROW_NUMBER() to tag records, filter to row_number==1 for non-SUM fields, and join back to the summed amounts. Additionally, add an explicit overflow check in _amount_to_fs12() that raises an error (or at minimum logs a warning) when abs(amount_fs) >= 10**12 for positive values or >= 10**11 for negative values, to prevent silent digit truncation. Remove or clearly caveat the pre-aggregation orderBy as it does not influence F.first() behaviour after a groupBy shuffle.
